FINAL IVX IA SENIOR DEVELOPER CLOSEOUT
EXECUTE ITEMS ONE BY ONE — DO NOT STOP UNTIL ALL EXECUTABLE ITEMS ARE COMPLETED, DEPLOYED, AND VERIFIED

THIS IS AN EXECUTION ORDER, NOT A REQUEST FOR ANOTHER AUDIT.

Do not return a large narrative before executing.
Do not repeat previously completed work unless fresh verification fails.
Do not mark PASS from source-code inspection alone when runtime, device, build, deployment, or live proof is required.
Do not replace missing execution with explanations.
Do not create comment-only, test-marker-only, label-only, or documentation-only proof.
Do not claim 100% while any critical item is FAILED, BLOCKED without exact owner action, NOT RUN, or UNVERIFIED.

Continue automatically from one item to the next.

Only pause when:

1. An owner approval phrase is legally required.
2. A verified credential returns 401/403, is missing, expired, deleted, or revoked.
3. A physical-device or external-console operation cannot technically be performed from the current environment.
4. Continuing could damage production data or exceed an approved safety threshold.

When paused, return only:

- exact item number;
- exact blocker;
- exact verification performed;
- exact owner action required;
- exact approval phrase if applicable;
- the next automatic action after approval.

Do not restart the full audit after approval. Resume from the blocked item.

==================================================
GLOBAL COMPLETION STANDARD
==================================================

Every item must have:

- item number;
- task ID;
- status;
- starting SHA;
- files inspected;
- files changed;
- tests executed;
- pass/fail/skip results;
- commit SHA where applicable;
- deployment ID where applicable;
- runtime SHA where applicable;
- APK/build evidence where applicable;
- live verification;
- trace ID;
- timestamp;
- proof-ledger record.

Allowed statuses:

NOT_STARTED
RUNNING
BLOCKED
FAILED
COMPLETED
NOT_APPLICABLE

One item receives one final status.
No “COMPLETED + BLOCKED.”
No “PASS with no evidence.”
No status inferred from narrative wording.

==================================================
STAGE 1 — FREEZE THE CURRENT BASELINE
ITEMS 1–15
==================================================

1. Confirm the canonical owner GitHub repository.
2. Confirm the production branch.
3. Record GitHub HEAD.
4. Record Render service ID.
5. Record Render runtime SHA.
6. Verify GitHub HEAD equals Render runtime SHA.
7. Record current production APK version.
8. Record current versionCode.
9. Record current APK URL.
10. Record current APK SHA-256.
11. Record production landing URL and ETag.
12. Record Supabase project ID.
13. Record current automated-test totals.
14. Record all current FAILED/BLOCKED/NOT_RUN items.
15. Create one durable closeout ledger and use it for this entire execution.

Required baseline output:

REPOSITORY:
BRANCH:
GITHUB_HEAD:
RENDER_SERVICE:
RUNTIME_SHA:
SHA_MATCH:
CURRENT_APK:
VERSION:
VERSION_CODE:
APK_SHA256:
LANDING_ETAG:
SUPABASE_PROJECT:
OPEN_CRITICAL_ITEMS:
LEDGER_ID:

==================================================
STAGE 2 — CLEAN EXECUTION ENVIRONMENT
ITEMS 16–30
==================================================

16. Create a fresh clone from owner GitHub.
17. Confirm clean worktree.
18. Verify Node version.
19. Verify Bun version.
20. Verify Expo SDK version.
21. Verify React Native version.
22. Verify TypeScript version.
23. Run clean dependency installation.
24. Verify lockfile consistency.
25. Install and resolve the required AI SDK/package.
26. Run clean backend dependency test.
27. Run clean Expo dependency test.
28. Verify no package is resolved only from a Rork-local cache.
29. Verify no hidden local patch exists.
30. Save clean-environment evidence.

If `expo/node_modules` is missing, install dependencies and continue. Do not mark the clean install FAIL merely because dependencies had not yet been installed.

==================================================
STAGE 3 — RORK INDEPENDENCE AND OWNER CONTROL
ITEMS 31–50
==================================================

31. Verify no `@rork-ai` runtime SDK is installed.
32. Verify no Rork Metro wrapper is active.
33. Verify no Rork proxy is required by production.
34. Verify no Rork runtime URL is called.
35. Verify no Rork package/bundle identifier remains.
36. Verify no runtime-visible Rork branding remains in IVX IA Chat.
37. Verify GitHub is owner-controlled.
38. Verify Render deploy source points to owner GitHub.
39. Verify Supabase is owner-controlled.
40. Verify AWS/S3/CloudFront are owner-controlled.
41. Verify Expo/EAS ownership.
42. Verify Android signing ownership.
43. Verify Apple project ownership where available.
44. Verify GitHub writes require owner approval.
45. Verify Render deployment requires owner approval.
46. Verify Supabase migration requires owner approval.
47. Verify APK upload requires owner approval.
48. Verify destructive actions require owner approval.
49. Verify approval tokens are scoped, expiring, and single-use.
50. Verify Rork cannot perform an owner-gated action without approval.

Owner approvals must never grant permanent unrestricted access.

==================================================
STAGE 4 — IVX IA CHAT ROUTING
ITEMS 51–70
==================================================

51. Route explanation requests to READ_ONLY.
52. Route inspection requests to READ_ONLY.
53. Route status requests to STATUS_ONLY.
54. Route QA requests to QA_ONLY.
55. Route “find and fix” to CODE_CHANGE.
56. Route implementation requests to CODE_CHANGE.
57. Route refactors to CODE_CHANGE.
58. Route existing-commit deployment to DEPLOY_ONLY.
59. Route module creation to CREATE_MODULE.
60. Route independent app creation to CREATE_APP.
61. Route schema/migration requests to DATABASE_CHANGE.
62. Route APK creation to BUILD.
63. Route rollback to ROLLBACK.
64. Route destructive requests to DANGEROUS_ACTION.
65. Reject destructive execution without approval.
66. Prevent CODE_CHANGE from becoming deploy-only.
67. Prevent QA_ONLY from editing files.
68. Prevent READ_ONLY from editing files.
69. Prevent STATUS_ONLY from creating duplicate tasks.
70. Run and pass the complete routing test suite.

==================================================
STAGE 5 — TASK STATE MACHINE AND CHAT TRUTHFULNESS
ITEMS 71–95
==================================================

71. Create one stable task ID per request.
72. Persist prompt hash.
73. Persist execution mode.
74. Persist repository and branch.
75. Persist starting SHA.
76. Support QUEUED.
77. Support INSPECTING.
78. Support PLANNING.
79. Support PATCHING.
80. Support TESTING.
81. Support REVISING.
82. Support TYPECHECKING.
83. Support COMMITTING.
84. Support BUILDING.
85. Support DEPLOYING.
86. Support VERIFYING.
87. Support COMPLETED.
88. Support FAILED.
89. Support BLOCKED.
90. Support CANCELLED.
91. Support ROLLED_BACK.
92. Enforce one terminal status.
93. Prohibit contradictory statuses.
94. Prevent duplicate assistant completion messages.
95. Verify latest task and latest message open correctly in IVX IA Chat.

==================================================
STAGE 6 — PROOF LEDGER AND FAKE-EXECUTION PROTECTION
ITEMS 96–115
==================================================

96. Require task ID for every execution claim.
97. Require starting SHA.
98. Require files inspected.
99. Require files changed.
100. Require test command and results.
101. Require TypeScript result.
102. Require lint result.
103. Require commit SHA for committed changes.
104. Require deploy ID for deployments.
105. Require runtime SHA for live verification.
106. Require HTTP result or equivalent production evidence.
107. Require commit/runtime parity.
108. Require trace IDs.
109. Require owner approval evidence.
110. Reject missing proof fields.
111. Reject fabricated file lists.
112. Reject fabricated deployment claims.
113. Reject “done” without executable evidence.
114. Save immutable proof records.
115. Run fake-execution and proof-standard tests with zero critical failures.

==================================================
STAGE 7 — FRESH REAL BUG-FIX CERTIFICATION
ITEMS 116–140
==================================================

This closes critical certification Item 298.

116. Select one controlled real behavioral defect.
117. Create the task from IVX IA Chat.
118. Reproduce the defect.
119. Capture pre-fix behavior.
120. Identify the exact root cause.
121. Identify the exact source file/function.
122. Add a failing regression test.
123. Confirm the test fails before the patch.
124. Generate a meaningful patch through the autonomous coder.
125. Reject comment-only or marker-only changes.
126. Apply the patch.
127. Run targeted tests.
128. Parse failures automatically.
129. Revise autonomously if necessary.
130. Pass the targeted tests.
131. Pass related regression tests.
132. Pass TypeScript.
133. Pass lint.
134. Pass security checks.
135. Request owner GitHub approval.
136. Commit through the IVX execution path.
137. Request owner deployment approval.
138. Deploy.
139. Verify production behavior changed.
140. Mark the task COMPLETED with a fresh proof-ledger record.

Required approval phrases when reached:

CONFIRM_IVX_GITHUB_WRITE
CONFIRM_IVX_RENDER_DEPLOY

Required proof:

TASK_ID:
DEFECT:
ROOT_CAUSE:
TEST_BEFORE:
FILES_CHANGED:
TEST_AFTER:
COMMIT_SHA:
DEPLOY_ID:
RUNTIME_SHA:
LIVE_RESULT:
TRACE_ID:

==================================================
STAGE 8 — QA-ONLY CERTIFICATION
ITEMS 141–155
==================================================

141. Start a QA-only task from chat.
142. Select relevant modules automatically.
143. Select relevant unit tests.
144. Select relevant integration tests.
145. Select relevant API contract tests.
146. Run scoped TypeScript.
147. Run applicable lint.
148. Run health probes.
149. Run authorization probes.
150. Return pass/fail/skip counts.
151. Verify zero changed files.
152. Verify no commit.
153. Verify no deployment.
154. Return one terminal QA result.
155. Save QA evidence in the ledger.

==================================================
STAGE 9 — AUTONOMOUS REVISION AND SELF-REPAIR
ITEMS 156–170
==================================================

156. Seed a safe controlled first-patch failure.
157. Generate the first patch.
158. Run the targeted test.
159. Capture the failure.
160. Parse the exact assertion/error.
161. Generate a second patch autonomously.
162. Confirm no human/Rork authored the correction.
163. Re-run the targeted test.
164. Run related regression tests.
165. Pass TypeScript.
166. Pass lint.
167. Enforce maximum revision count.
168. Enforce model-call/token/runtime limits.
169. Commit the successful revision after approval.
170. Save complete iteration evidence.

==================================================
STAGE 10 — FRESH IVX MODULE CREATION
ITEMS 171–205
==================================================

This closes critical certification Item 299.

Create a real integrated module from IVX IA Chat:

MODULE: Investor Performance Center

171. Submit the module request through IVX IA Chat.
172. Create a fresh task ID.
173. Inspect current IVX architecture.
174. Generate an implementation plan.
175. Create an active route.
176. Add navigation.
177. Create typed frontend models.
178. Create typed API contracts.
179. Create the backend endpoint.
180. Add database migration only if required.
181. Add RLS if required.
182. Add owner authorization.
183. Add investor authorization.
184. Add loading state.
185. Add cached-data state.
186. Add empty state.
187. Add partial-error state.
188. Add fatal-error state.
189. Add search.
190. Add filters.
191. Add pagination.
192. Display real investor data contracts.
193. Display invested capital.
194. Display active deals.
195. Display distributions.
196. Display unrealized value.
197. Display realized return.
198. Display ROI.
199. Display last activity.
200. Apply official IVX branding.
201. Add unit and integration tests.
202. Pass TypeScript and lint.
203. Commit after owner approval.
204. Deploy after owner approval.
205. Open the module in production and capture live evidence.

Do not count disconnected factory code as the module.
The module must be accessible inside the active IVX production application.

==================================================
STAGE 11 — FRESH INDEPENDENT APP CREATION
ITEMS 206–245
==================================================

This closes critical certification Item 300.

APP: IVX Property Inspection

206. Request repository creation approval.
207. Create an owner-controlled GitHub repository.
208. Verify repository ownership.
209. Configure default branch.
210. Configure branch protection.
211. Generate an Expo Router app.
212. Use TypeScript.
213. Apply official IVX branding.
214. Generate unique Android package name.
215. Generate unique iOS bundle ID.
216. Create backend structure.
217. Create shared types.
218. Create environment template.
219. Add authentication.
220. Add inspector role.
221. Add owner/admin role.
222. Create property list.
223. Create inspection workflow.
224. Create room checklist.
225. Create notes.
226. Create photo upload.
227. Create condition rating.
228. Create issue severity.
229. Add offline drafts.
230. Add reconnect synchronization.
231. Add submission workflow.
232. Add inspection summary.
233. Create Supabase schema/project after approval.
234. Create migrations.
235. Add indexes and foreign keys.
236. Add RLS policies.
237. Add tests.
238. Pass TypeScript.
239. Pass lint.
240. Add CI.
241. Add backend deployment configuration.
242. Build the web/admin portal.
243. Deploy the backend/web portal.
244. Build an installable Android APK.
245. Return repository, URL, APK, checksums, screenshots, and no-Rork proof.

Approvals when reached:

CONFIRM_IVX_CREATE_REPOSITORY
CONFIRM_IVX_SUPABASE_MIGRATION
CONFIRM_IVX_GITHUB_WRITE
CONFIRM_IVX_RENDER_DEPLOY
CONFIRM_IVX_APK_UPLOAD

==================================================
STAGE 12 — CURRENT IVX MOBILE APK CLOSEOUT
ITEMS 246–270
==================================================

246. Confirm all pending mobile source fixes are committed.
247. Verify QueryClient improvements.
248. Verify `DealVideoCard` uses `expo-image`.
249. Verify `HoldingCard` uses `expo-image`.
250. Verify `TrustDealCard` uses `expo-image`.
251. Verify Home skeleton loading.
252. Verify CRM skeleton loading.
253. Verify Invest hardcoded colors = 0.
254. Verify Profit/Loss hardcoded colors = 0.
255. Verify IVX IA Chat branding.
256. Verify business/document branding.
257. Verify App Factory branding inheritance.
258. Select the next unused version.
259. Select the next unused versionCode.
260. Update all version sources consistently.
261. Run clean Expo dependency install.
262. Run clean Gradle build.
263. Ensure JS bundling reaches 100%.
264. Produce signed APK.
265. Calculate APK SHA-256.
266. Upload to owner-controlled distribution.
267. Verify HTTP 200, size, ETag, and hash.
268. Download the APK.
269. Install it on a physical Android device.
270. Launch it and capture version + screenshots.

Do not call the new APK complete if no APK file exists.

==================================================
STAGE 13 — AUTHENTICATION, SMTP, AND RECOVERY
ITEMS 271–300
==================================================

271. Check stored SMTP variables before requesting anything.
272. Verify SMTP host.
273. Verify SMTP port.
274. Verify SMTP username.
275. Verify SMTP secret binding.
276. Verify sender email and sender domain.
277. Configure SMTP if variables exist.
278. Configure SPF.
279. Configure DKIM.
280. Configure DMARC.
281. Send confirmation email.
282. Verify confirmation link.
283. Send forgot-password email.
284. Verify reset link.
285. Reset password.
286. Confirm new password works.
287. Confirm old password fails.
288. Confirm reused reset link fails.
289. Test resend confirmation.
290. Test owner login.
291. Test member login.
292. Test invalid password.
293. Test logout/login.
294. Test session persistence after restart.
295. Test token refresh.
296. Test network loss/reconnect.
297. Test Samsung Browser.
298. Test Android Chrome.
299. Test available iPhone/desktop browsers.
300. Confirm MFA remains optional and OFF by default unless owner enables it.

==================================================
STAGE 14 — PHYSICAL REELS AND DEVICE QA
ITEMS 301–325
==================================================

301. Run Reels for 60 continuous minutes.
302. Execute 500 scroll transitions.
303. Execute 200 viewer open/close cycles.
304. Execute 100 background/foreground cycles.
305. Execute network-off/on transitions.
306. Execute Wi-Fi/cellular transitions where possible.
307. Test rapid swipe.
308. Test reverse swipe.
309. Test pause/resume.
310. Test mute/unmute.
311. Test comments open/close.
312. Test app restart and return to Reels.
313. Record crash count.
314. Record ANR count.
315. Record peak memory.
316. Record final memory.
317. Record memory growth.
318. Record CPU.
319. Record FPS.
320. Record JS-thread stalls.
321. Record native-thread stalls.
322. Record active-player maximum.
323. Record frozen players/black frames.
324. Record duplicate-video count.
325. Verify recovery after reconnect.

Physical-device proof is required.
Code-level simulation is not a substitute.

==================================================
STAGE 15 — LOAD, RATE LIMITS, AND PERFORMANCE
ITEMS 326–345
==================================================

326. Verify login rate limit.
327. Verify registration rate limit.
328. Verify password-recovery rate limit.
329. Verify IVX IA Chat rate limit.
330. Verify upload rate limit.
331. Verify HTTP 429.
332. Verify Retry-After.
333. Run 100 concurrent-user test.
334. Run 500 concurrent-user test.
335. Run 1,000 concurrent-user test.
336. Run 5,000 concurrent-user test safely.
337. Run 10,000 concurrent-user test safely or stop at documented safety threshold.
338. Measure p50.
339. Measure p95.
340. Measure p99.
341. Measure error rate.
342. Measure database connections/query latency.
343. Measure Render CPU/memory.
344. Verify recovery after load.
345. Save complete performance evidence.

Use an owner-controlled cloud VM/load-testing service.
Do not run unsafe destructive traffic.

==================================================
STAGE 16 — LIVE ROLLBACK DRILL
ITEMS 346–355
==================================================

346. Create a safe visible test change.
347. Commit after approval.
348. Deploy after approval.
349. Verify the test change live.
350. Identify previous healthy SHA.
351. Request rollback approval.
352. Execute live rollback.
353. Verify previous SHA and behavior.
354. Re-deploy the final healthy release.
355. Verify final runtime and save rollback evidence.

Required approval:

CONFIRM_IVX_ROLLBACK

Rollback unit tests alone do not qualify.

==================================================
STAGE 17 — FINAL MODULE-BY-MODULE QA
ITEMS 356–380
==================================================

==================================================
STAGE 18 — FINAL CLEAN TEST SUITE
ITEMS 381–395
==================================================

381. Run routing tests.
382. Run state-machine tests.
383. Run fake-execution tests.
384. Run proof-ledger tests.
385. Run autonomous-coder tests.
386. Run worker/recovery tests.

Acceptance:

==================================================
STAGE 19 — FINAL PRODUCTION PARITY
ITEMS 396–400
==================================================

396. Verify GitHub HEAD equals Render runtime SHA.

398. Verify landing asset hashes match deployed assets.
